title: Stop autoSelectedProfileId's build() from writing to the DB and mutating sibling providers

evidence.quote:
// Stale id — clear it and fall through to the auto-select/self-heal path.
    ref.read(selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier).clear();

why: autoSelectedProfileId's build() function calls `selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier.clear()`/`.select(id)` (mutating a sibling provider), `ref.invalidate(profileListProvider)`, and `repo.ensureDefaultProfile(...)` (which inserts a new learner_profiles row and re-parents orphaned rows) — all from inside a provider's build(). This is a deliberate, heavily-commented fix for BUG D1 (self-healing a profile-less authenticated account), and the fast path is idempotent, so it is not causing an active bug. But it does mean merely watching/reading this provider can trigger a database write, which is surprising for what looks like a plain derived value and makes the provider harder to unit-test without a real (or faked) UserDatabase.
recommendation: Move the self-heal side effect out of build() into an explicit ref.listen-driven effect (e.g. in app_shell.dart, which already watches auth state) or a widget-triggered callback, keeping build() a pure read.
acceptance_criteria: autoSelectedProfileId's build() (or its replacement) contains no writes to other providers or the database; existing BUG D1 self-heal tests keep passing

corrections: Both evidence line numbers are off by one: comment '// Stale id...' is at line 97 not 98 (clear() is at 98); 'id = await repo.ensureDefaultProfile(' is at line 110 not 109. Quoted text is verbatim-correct, just a citation slip, not fabrication.
